# Model and source

Hong 2026 reports the exposure-response (ER) analyses supporting the
datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) dose of 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks in previously
treated advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Efficacy was analysed in
644 NSCLC patients and safety in 729 patients (the same 644 plus 85 breast
cancer patients) pooled from TROPION-PanTumor01, TROPION-Lung05 and
TROPION-Lung01. Six of the paper's endpoints are packaged here:

```{r models}
erModels <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Model,                                  ~Endpoint,                            ~Method,                         ~`Exposure metric`,      ~Output,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_os",              "Overall survival",                   "Gompertz time-to-event",        "Dato-DXd AUC1",         "hazard, sur",
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_pfs",             "Progression-free survival",          "Exponential time-to-event",     "Dato-DXd AUCtau (time-varying)", "hazard, sur",
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_orr",             "Objective response (BICR)",          "Logistic, Emax",                "Dato-DXd Cav (ug/mL)",  "prob_orr_central",
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3",     "Grade 3+ TEAE",                      "Logistic, linear",              "DXd Cav (ng/mL)",       "prob_teae_grade3",
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_sae",             "Serious TEAE",                       "Logistic, linear",              "DXd Cav (ng/mL)",       "prob_sae",
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction",  "TEAE leading to dose reduction",     "Logistic, linear",              "Dato-DXd AUC1",         "prob_dose_reduction"
)
knitr::kable(erModels, caption = "The six packaged Hong 2026 models.")
```

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hong_2026_datopotamab_os"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.70477> (open access, PMC13572793)
* The individual exposures were empirical Bayes predictions from the population
  PK model of Hong 2025, packaged as `Hong_2025_datopotamab`.

**How complete each model is.** The two survival models are the paper's final
models, transcribed from Table 2 (overall survival) and Supplementary Table S4
(progression-free survival). The four logistic models are a different kind of
object. Hong 2026 prints no intercept or exposure coefficient for any logistic
model -- only the ORR EC50 and the covariate odds ratios of the final models.
What it does plot (Figures 3 and 4) is the curve of each endpoint's **drug-effect
model**, the exposure-only model fitted before covariate selection. Those curves
were digitised and the intercept and slope back-solved, so the four packaged
logistic models are the exposure-only drug-effect models. The final-model
covariate odds ratios are listed in the Assumptions section but not encoded,
because adding them to an intercept from a different model would describe
neither.

**Endpoints not packaged.** The five adverse-event-of-special-interest
time-to-event models (any-grade and grade 2+ oral mucositis/stomatitis,
any-grade and grade 2+ ocular surface toxicity, adjudicated drug-related
ILD/pneumonitis) are summarised in Table 3 only as covariate hazard ratios; no
baseline hazard, Gompertz shape or exposure coefficient is printed or plotted,
so they cannot be reconstructed.

None of the six models has a dose: the exposure metric is a data column.
`AUC_DATODXD` is the Cycle-1 AUC of intact Dato-DXd and `AUC_DATODXD_TAU` the
cycle-wise AUC over each dosing interval; both are supplied in ug*day/mL and
converted inside the model to the paper's mg*h/mL (multiply by 24 / 1000).
**`CAV` carries two different analytes**: intact Dato-DXd in ug/mL for the ORR
model and the released payload DXd in ng/mL for the two TEAE models.

# Source trace

| Model | Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| os | baseline hazard; Gompertz shape | 0.412 /year; 0.434 /year | Table 2 |
| os | AUC1 slope | -0.0216 per mg*h/mL | Table 2 |
| os | albumin; tumour size | -0.0612 per g/L; 0.00477 per mm | Table 2 |
| os | ECOG > 0; squamous; liver metastasis; female | 0.569; 0.393; 0.411; -0.279 | Table 2 |
| os | covariate centring | albumin 38 g/L, tumour size 67 mm | Figure 2 reference patient; Table S3 medians |
| pfs | baseline hazard | 5.85 /year | Table S4 |
| pfs | Emax; EC50 of AUCtau | -3.45; 17.6 mg*h/mL | Table S4 |
| pfs | age; albumin | -0.0156 per year; 0.0266 per g/L applied as -0.0266 | Table S4; sign from Table 1 and Figure S2 |
| pfs | squamous; last prior IO; liver metastasis; female | 0.598; -0.303; 0.537; -0.312 | Table S4 |
| pfs | covariate centring | age 63 y, albumin 38 g/L | Figure S2 reference patient |
| os, pfs | h(t) = h0(t) exp(f(Exposure) + sum beta_i X_i) | -- | Supplementary Equation S1 |
| orr | EC50 | 0.00404 mg/mL = 4.04 ug/mL | Results, ORR |
| orr | intercept; Emax | -7.845; 8.001 | back-solved from the Figure 3 curve |
| teae_grade3 | intercept; DXd Cav slope | -1.092; 1.441 per ng/mL | back-solved from Figure 4, top left |
| sae | intercept; DXd Cav slope | -1.851; 1.487 per ng/mL | back-solved from Figure 4, top right |
| dose_reduction | intercept; AUC1 slope | -3.263; 0.1081 per mg*h/mL | back-solved from Figure 4, bottom |
| all logistic | logit(P) = logit(Pbase) + f(Exposure) | -- | Supplementary Equation S2 |

# Structural checks: hazard ratios of the survival models

Table 1, Figure 2 (overall survival) and Figure S2 (progression-free survival)
print hazard ratios against a reference patient. Each survival model is solved
for the two patients at one time point and the hazard ratio compared with the
printed value. Because the hazards are proportional, the ratio does not depend
on the time chosen. The printed values are medians over 250 parameter vectors
drawn from the estimates' uncertainty, so they can differ slightly from the
ratio at the point estimates.

```{r helpers}
# Solve a model for several virtual patients at a single time (one row per
# patient); covariates are columns of `covs`, one row per patient.
solveRows <- function(modelName, covs, time = 0.5) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_len(nrow(covs)), time = time, amt = 0, evid = 0L)
  ev <- cbind(ev, covs)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
    rxode2::rxode(readModelDb(modelName)),
    events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"
  ))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == nrow(covs))
  s
}

refOs <- data.frame(
  AUC_DATODXD = 15.2 * 1000 / 24, ALB = 38, TUMSZ = 67,
  ECOG_GE1 = 0, TUMTP_NSCLC_SQUAM = 0, LMET = 0, SEXF = 0
)
refPfs <- data.frame(
  AUC_DATODXD_TAU = 13.9 * 1000 / 24, AGE = 63, ALB = 38,
  TUMTP_NSCLC_SQUAM = 0, LAST_PRIOR_IO = 0, LMET = 0, SEXF = 0
)
hrTable <- function(modelName, ref, changes) {
  rows <- lapply(changes, function(ch) {
    alt <- ref
    for (nm in names(ch$set)) alt[[nm]] <- ch$set[[nm]]
    h <- solveRows(modelName, rbind(ref, alt))$hazard
    data.frame(Comparison = ch$label, Printed = ch$printed, Model = signif(h[2] / h[1], 3))
  })
  out <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  out$`Diff (%)` <- round(100 * (out$Model / out$Printed - 1), 1)
  out
}
mghml <- function(x) x * 1000 / 24 # mg*h/mL -> ug*day/mL
```

```{r hr-os}
hrOs <- hrTable("Hong_2026_datopotamab_os", refOs, list(
  list(label = "AUC1 7.38 vs 15.2 mg*h/mL", set = list(AUC_DATODXD = mghml(7.38)), printed = 1.17),
  list(label = "AUC1 25.3 vs 15.2 mg*h/mL", set = list(AUC_DATODXD = mghml(25.3)), printed = 0.814),

  list(label = "8 mg/kg median AUC1 21.4", set = list(AUC_DATODXD = mghml(21.4)), printed = 0.881),
  list(label = "ECOG > 0", set = list(ECOG_GE1 = 1), printed = 1.80),
  list(label = "Albumin 28.0 vs 38 g/L", set = list(ALB = 28), printed = 1.84),
  list(label = "Albumin 45.0 vs 38 g/L", set = list(ALB = 45), printed = 0.652),
  list(label = "Female sex", set = list(SEXF = 1), printed = 0.768),

knitr::kable(hrOs, caption = "Overall survival: model hazard ratios against Table 1 and Figure 2.")
```

```{r hr-assert}
# Every covariate and the near-reference exposure rows match to within 5%.
# The PFS AUCtau rows at the 5th and 95th percentiles differ by 17% and 9%: they
# sit far from the reference on the curved part of an Emax function whose EC50
# has a 41.9% RSE, where the median over uncertainty draws departs from the
# point estimate. Both still move in the printed direction.
nearRef <- !grepl("2.52|26.9", hrPfs$Comparison)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(hrOs$`Diff (%)`) < 5),
  all(abs(hrPfs$`Diff (%)`[nearRef]) < 5),
  all(abs(hrPfs$`Diff (%)`[!nearRef]) < 20),
  all(sign(log(hrPfs$Model)) == sign(log(hrPfs$Printed)))
)
```

The albumin rows of the progression-free survival model are the check behind
its one deviation from the printed table: Supplementary Table S4 prints the
albumin coefficient as +0.0266 per g/L, which would make the hazard *rise* with
albumin, whereas Table 1, Figure S2 and the Results all report the opposite.
With the sign applied as negative the model reproduces all four printed albumin
hazard ratios.

# Structural checks: the Discussion's 6 versus 4 mg/kg contrasts

The Discussion states that, compared with 4 mg/kg, 6 mg/kg was predicted to
reduce the risk of death by 10%, the risk of progression or death by 22%, and
to increase the odds of objective response by 35%. The median exposures of the
two dose groups from Figures 2, S2 and S3 reproduce the first two through the
survival models.

```{r discussion}
osDose <- solveRows("Hong_2026_datopotamab_os", rbind(
  transform(refOs, AUC_DATODXD = mghml(10.2)),
  transform(refOs, AUC_DATODXD = mghml(15.2))
))$hazard
pfsDose <- solveRows("Hong_2026_datopotamab_pfs", rbind(
  transform(refPfs, AUC_DATODXD_TAU = mghml(10.2)),
  transform(refPfs, AUC_DATODXD_TAU = mghml(13.9))
))$hazard
orrDose <- solveRows("Hong_2026_datopotamab_orr", data.frame(CAV = c(20.7, 28.9)))$prob_orr_central
odds <- function(p) p / (1 - p)
contrast <- data.frame(
  Contrast = c(
    "Overall survival: risk reduction",
    "Progression-free survival: risk reduction",
    "Objective response: odds increase"
  ),
  Printed = c(10, 22, 35),
  Model = round(c(
    100 * (1 - osDose[2] / osDose[1]),
    100 * (1 - pfsDose[2] / pfsDose[1]),
    100 * (odds(orrDose[2]) / odds(orrDose[1]) - 1)
  ), 1)
)
knitr::kable(contrast, caption = "6 mg/kg versus 4 mg/kg at the dose-group median exposures (percent).")
stopifnot(abs(contrast$Model[1:2] - contrast$Printed[1:2]) < 1.5)
```

The objective-response contrast is 38% here rather than 35% because the packaged
ORR model is the drug-effect model (Emax 8.00 on the logit). The odds ratios of
the final ORR model printed in Figure S3 imply Emax = 7.48 with the same EC50,
which gives the paper's 35%:

```{r orr-final-emax}
gEmax <- function(cav) cav / (4.04 + cav)
figS3 <- data.frame(
  cav = c(13.0, 22.5, 36.0, 52.6, 20.7, 40.7),
  or = c(0.426, 0.802, 1.18, 1.47, 0.738, 1.27)
)
figS3$impliedEmax <- log(figS3$or) / (gEmax(figS3$cav) - gEmax(28.9))
figS3 |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dato-DXd Cav (ug/mL)" = cav,
    "Printed OR vs 28.9 ug/mL" = or,
    "Implied logit Emax" = impliedEmax
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Figure S3 odds ratios of the final ORR model and the Emax each implies at EC50 = 4.04 ug/mL.")
```

```{r orr-final-assert}
stopifnot(abs(mean(figS3$impliedEmax) - 7.48) < 0.1, sd(figS3$impliedEmax) < 0.15)
```

The six rows agree on one Emax, which confirms that the printed EC50 belongs to
the final model and that the Emax form is read correctly; it also shows the
final model's Emax is 7% smaller than the drug-effect model's.

# Virtual cohort

A virtual cohort of 200 patients per dose group (4, 6 and 8 mg/kg) draws its
covariates from the Table S3 distributions. Individual exposures are lognormal
around the dose-group medians of Figures 2 and S2, with the spread implied by the
6 mg/kg 5th and 95th AUC1 percentiles (7.38 and 25.3 mg*h/mL, a log-scale SD of
0.374); the same spread is assumed for AUCtau. AUCtau is held at each patient's
mean value throughout follow-up.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261117)
set.seed(20261117)
nPerArm <- 200
cohort <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(3 * nPerArm),
  dose = rep(c("4 mg/kg", "6 mg/kg", "8 mg/kg"), each = nPerArm),
  auc1Med = rep(c(10.2, 15.2, 21.4), each = nPerArm),
  auctauMed = rep(c(10.2, 13.9, 18.0), each = nPerArm),
  z = rnorm(3 * nPerArm),
  AGE = pmin(pmax(rnorm(3 * nPerArm, 61.6, 10.3), 26), 84),
  ALB = pmin(pmax(rnorm(3 * nPerArm, 37.4, 5.10), 19), 50),
  TUMSZ = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(3 * nPerArm, log(67), 0.6)), 13), 314),
  ECOG_GE1 = rbinom(3 * nPerArm, 1, 0.71),
  SEXF = rbinom(3 * nPerArm, 1, 0.458),
  LMET = rbinom(3 * nPerArm, 1, 0.23),
  TUMTP_NSCLC_SQUAM = rbinom(3 * nPerArm, 1, 0.15),
  LAST_PRIOR_IO = rbinom(3 * nPerArm, 1, 0.54)
) |>
  mutate(
    AUC_DATODXD = mghml(auc1Med * exp(0.374 * z)),
    AUC_DATODXD_TAU = mghml(auctauMed * exp(0.374 * z))
  )
```

# Simulated overall and progression-free survival

The survival models are solved on a grid of 0 to 3 years. Each patient's
survival curve is deterministic given the covariates; the population curve is
their average.

```{r tte-solve}
timeGrid <- seq(0, 3, by = 1 / 52)
tteEvents <- tidyr::crossing(
  cohort |> select(-z, -auc1Med, -auctauMed, -dose),
  time = timeGrid
) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L) |>
  arrange(id, time)

osSim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hong_2026_datopotamab_os")),
  events = tteEvents, returnType = "data.frame"
)) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, dose), by = "id")
pfsSim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Hong_2026_datopotamab_pfs")),
  events = tteEvents, returnType = "data.frame"
)) |>
  left_join(cohort |> select(id, dose), by = "id")
stopifnot(!anyNA(osSim$sur), !anyNA(pfsSim$sur))

popCurve <- function(sim, endpoint) {
  sim |>
    group_by(dose, time) |>
    summarise(sur = mean(sur), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(endpoint = endpoint)
}
curves <- bind_rows(popCurve(osSim, "Overall survival"), popCurve(pfsSim, "Progression-free survival"))
medianDays <- function(cv) {
  cv |>
    group_by(endpoint, dose) |>
    summarise(`Median (days)` = round(365.25 * approx(rev(sur), rev(time), xout = 0.5)$y), .groups = "drop")
}
medians <- medianDays(curves)
knitr::kable(medians, caption = "Model-predicted median survival of the virtual cohort.")
```

```{r tte-plot, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(curves, aes(time * 365.25, 100 * sur, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since first dose (days)", y = "Patients without event (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Compare with Figure 1 of Hong 2026 (observed Kaplan-Meier curves by exposure quartile)."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Figure 1 of Hong 2026 shows the observed pooled curves: overall survival falls
through 50% at roughly 230 days in the lowest AUC1 quartile and roughly 500 days
in the highest, and progression-free survival at roughly 100 to 230 days across
quartiles. The 6 mg/kg cohort lies inside both ranges. This check is what
supports two structural readings that the paper does not state outright: that
the overall-survival exposure term is uncentred (centring it at the reference
AUC1 shortens the predicted median by about a quarter) and that age and albumin
are centred at their medians.

```{r tte-assert}
os6 <- medians$`Median (days)`[medians$endpoint == "Overall survival" & medians$dose == "6 mg/kg"]
pfs6 <- medians$`Median (days)`[medians$endpoint == "Progression-free survival" & medians$dose == "6 mg/kg"]
stopifnot(os6 > 250, os6 < 550, pfs6 > 100, pfs6 < 300)
```

# Logistic models against the observed exposure quartiles

Figures 3 and 4 plot the observed proportion of patients with the event in each
exposure quartile at the quartile's mean exposure; the mean exposures below were
read from the figures. The packaged drug-effect models are evaluated at those
exposures.

```{r logistic}
obsQ <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Model,                                 ~Output,               ~Covariate,    ~x,    ~n,  ~N,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_orr",            "prob_orr_central",    "CAV",         16.2,  24,  148,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_orr",            "prob_orr_central",    "CAV",         26.0,  46,  148,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_orr",            "prob_orr_central",    "CAV",         32.4,  49,  148,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_orr",            "prob_orr_central",    "CAV",         46.2,  55,  148,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3",    "prob_teae_grade3",    "CAV",         0.337, 64,  188,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3",    "prob_teae_grade3",    "CAV",         0.515, 75,  180,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3",    "prob_teae_grade3",    "CAV",         0.679, 82,  184,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3",    "prob_teae_grade3",    "CAV",         1.228, 120, 177,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_sae",            "prob_sae",            "CAV",         0.331, 35,  197,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_sae",            "prob_sae",            "CAV",         0.499, 45,  176,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_sae",            "prob_sae",            "CAV",         0.650, 46,  176,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_sae",            "prob_sae",            "CAV",         1.159, 91,  180,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction", "prob_dose_reduction", "AUC_DATODXD", 9.36,  18,  183,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction", "prob_dose_reduction", "AUC_DATODXD", 14.21, 28,  182,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction", "prob_dose_reduction", "AUC_DATODXD", 17.21, 37,  182,
  "Hong_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction", "prob_dose_reduction", "AUC_DATODXD", 23.34, 57,  182
)
# Exposure units of the figures: ORR Cav in ug/mL (Figure 3 axis in mg/mL x
# 1000), DXd Cav in ng/mL, AUC1 in mg*h/mL (converted to ug*day/mL here).
obsQ$predicted <- NA_real_
for (m in unique(obsQ$Model)) {
  idx <- obsQ$Model == m
  cv <- obsQ$Covariate[idx][1]
  val <- obsQ$x[idx]
  if (cv == "AUC_DATODXD") val <- mghml(val)
  covs <- setNames(data.frame(val), cv)
  obsQ$predicted[idx] <- solveRows(m, covs)[[obsQ$Output[idx][1]]]
}
obsQ <- obsQ |> mutate(observed = n / N, diff = predicted - observed)
obsQ |>
  mutate(across(c(observed, predicted, diff), \(v) round(v, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Quartile mean exposure" = x, "Events" = n, "Patients" = N) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Observed quartile proportions (Figures 3 and 4) against the packaged models.")
stopifnot(all(abs(obsQ$diff) < 0.06))
```

```{r logistic-plot, fig.height = 6}
curveGrid <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(Model = "Hong_2026_datopotamab_orr", Output = "prob_orr_central", Covariate = "CAV", x = seq(0, 80, length.out = 81)),
  tibble::tibble(Model = "Hong_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3", Output = "prob_teae_grade3", Covariate = "CAV", x = seq(0, 1.4, length.out = 71)),
  tibble::tibble(Model = "Hong_2026_datopotamab_sae", Output = "prob_sae", Covariate = "CAV", x = seq(0, 1.4, length.out = 71)),
  tibble::tibble(Model = "Hong_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction", Output = "prob_dose_reduction", Covariate = "AUC_DATODXD", x = seq(0, 40, length.out = 81))
)
curveGrid$p <- NA_real_
for (m in unique(curveGrid$Model)) {
  idx <- curveGrid$Model == m
  cv <- curveGrid$Covariate[idx][1]
  val <- curveGrid$x[idx]
  if (cv == "AUC_DATODXD") val <- mghml(val)
  curveGrid$p[idx] <- solveRows(m, setNames(data.frame(val), cv))[[curveGrid$Output[idx][1]]]
}
xLab <- c(
  Hong_2026_datopotamab_orr = "ORR vs Dato-DXd Cav (ug/mL)",
  Hong_2026_datopotamab_teae_grade3 = "Grade 3+ TEAE vs DXd Cav (ng/mL)",
  Hong_2026_datopotamab_sae = "Serious TEAE vs DXd Cav (ng/mL)",
  Hong_2026_datopotamab_dose_reduction = "Dose-reduction TEAE vs Dato-DXd AUC1 (mg*h/mL)"
)
ggplot(curveGrid, aes(x, p)) +
```

# PKNCA

PKNCA does not apply: none of the six models has a pharmacokinetic layer or a
dose. Exposures come from the population PK model packaged as
`Hong_2025_datopotamab`, whose own article carries the NCA validation.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Logistic models are the drug-effect models, not the final models.** No
  logistic coefficient is printed except the ORR EC50. The intercepts and
  exposure coefficients were back-solved by least squares from the digitised
  model-predicted median curves of Figure 3 (ORR, read at Cav = 0.01 to 0.08
  mg/mL, EC50 held at 0.00404 mg/mL; largest residual 0.0075 logit) and Figure 4
  (the three TEAE panels, every pixel column of each curve; largest residual
  0.004 on the probability scale). The plotted curves are the exposure-only
  drug-effect models (Figure 3 and 4 captions), which is why they pass through
  the observed quartile proportions of the whole analysis population.
* **Final-model covariates of the logistic endpoints are not encoded.** Their
  odds ratios are printed (Tables 1 and 3) but the final-model intercept and
  exposure coefficient are not, and the drug-effect intercept is a
  population-average quantity, not the final model's reference patient. The
  printed odds ratios are: ORR, more than two prior lines of therapy 1.82 and
  squamous histology 0.281; grade 3+ TEAE, Asian race 0.566 and ECOG > 0 1.50;
  serious TEAE, ECOG > 0 2.14, squamous histology 1.68, breast cancer 0.380 and
  Asian race 0.504; dose-reduction TEAE, region Europe 2.20 and any renal
  impairment 1.90.
* **Albumin sign in the progression-free survival model.** Supplementary Table
  S4 prints +0.0266 per g/L; the model uses -0.0266 because Table 1, Figure S2
  and the Results all show the hazard falling as albumin rises, and the negative
  sign reproduces each printed albumin hazard ratio to within 1%.
* **Centring.** The paper does not state the centring of continuous
  covariates. Albumin (38 g/L), tumour size (67 mm) and age (63 years) are
  centred at the medians that define the reference patients of Figures 2 and
  S2 and that match Table S3. The exposure terms are uncentred: the
  progression-free survival Emax function is zero at zero exposure by
  construction, and an uncentred overall-survival slope reproduces the observed
  median survival of Figure 1 where a centred one does not.
* **EC50 unit.** Table S4 prints the progression-free survival EC50 unit as
  (mg/mL*h)^-1; an EC50 has the unit of its exposure, mg/mL*h.
* **AESI and ILD models are not packaged.** The five adverse-event-of-special
  interest time-to-event models are summarised only by covariate hazard ratios
  (Table 3); no baseline hazard, shape or exposure coefficient is reported, and
  ILD/pneumonitis showed no exposure-response relationship.
* **Virtual cohort.** Covariate distributions follow Table S3 (normal age and
  albumin, lognormal tumour size, independent binary covariates); exposures are
  lognormal around the printed dose-group medians with a common spread. AUCtau
  is constant per patient, a simplification of the cycle-wise metric, which the
  paper reports to show minimal accumulation.
* **No residual error.** The logistic models carry a placeholder additive
  residual (SD 0.001 on the probability) only so the nlmixr2 observation
  machinery accepts them; the source likelihoods are Bernoulli. The survival
  models declare no endpoint.
